key_insight: Large-scale tensor-network benchmarking shows that classical DMRG remains far more accurate and scalable than current NISQ quantum methods for the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model, especially as system size grows.
engineering_relevance: This work provides a practical benchmark for judging when quantum algorithms like VQE and SQD can compete with high-performance classical solvers on real hardware and large problem instances.
method: Used DMRG on the NERSC Perlmutter supercomputer to compute LMG ground-state energies.
Compared those classical results against VQE and SQD runs on an IBM Eagle quantum computer.
Evaluated accuracy across increasing particle counts to assess scaling under noisy hardware conditions.
evidence_signal: The dataset includes accurate ground-state energies up to 1400 particles; VQE stayed within 1% error only for 6 particles, while SQD extended that to 17 particles.
watch_item: The comparison is limited by noisy, hardware-specific quantum runs, so performance may change with improved error mitigation or more advanced devices.
paper_title: Benchmarking Quantum Simulations of the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick Model Using Large Tensor Networks
